cases.title: How a delivery text scam works

skeleton.brief: Introduce the scam message about undelivered parcel and fee
Explain timing targets people expecting parcels on Tuesday afternoons
Sender uses mobile number, unlike real couriers with registered short codes
Link mimics courier domain but controlled by scammer
Page requests £1.99, focusing on card details, not money
Follow-up call from bank fraud team to get verification code
Scam’s structure: small urgent ask followed by a trust-leveraging call
Why that sentence and scam design effectively trap victims

narration.text: The message says your parcel could not be delivered and asks for one small fee. Here is why that particular sentence works.

It arrives on a Tuesday afternoon, when a lot of people genuinely are expecting something. The scam does not need to be believable to everyone. It needs to be believable to the fraction who have a parcel out.

narration.text: Front doors reflect the character of a city. They reveal how people live, what matters to them, and how they solve everyday problems.

asset_request.description: a variety of city front doors from different cultures
asset_request.guidance: A clear, colorful shot showing diverse front doors from different cities, no people in frame.

slot_panel.heading: Front doors as reflections of city character
bullets: They show local culture and needs

narration.text: In Amsterdam, houses lean forward over canals. Their narrow, tall doors have hoisting beams at the top, used to lift furniture up tight staircases.

asset_request.description: an Amsterdam house front with a hoisting beam over the door
asset_request.guidance: A clean, centered photo of an Amsterdam canal house showing the hoisting beam clearly.

narration.text: Marrakesh doors are heavy and studded, with no windows. They face inward courtyards, protecting the family’s private space from the street.

asset_request.description: a heavy studded front door in Marrakesh with no windows
asset_request.guidance: A close-up of a traditional Marrakesh door showing studs and no windows.

narration.text: Kyoto doors use a wooden lattice screen in front, with sliding paper doors behind. This lets residents open the boundary to the street by just a hand’s width.

asset_request.description: a Kyoto wooden lattice screen and sliding paper door
asset_request.guidance: A detailed photo of a traditional Kyoto wooden lattice and paper sliding door.

narration.text: In Reykjavik, houses are wrapped in colorful corrugated iron. The bright reds, ochres, and teals help bring light during the long, dark winters when sunlight is scarce.

slot_main.heading: Key Point
bullets: In Reykjavik, houses are wrapped in colorful corrugated iron.

narration.text: Each city’s front doors solve local problems. Vernacular architecture is thousands of small adaptations, shaped by people living with what came before.

slot_main.heading: Doors shaped by local needs
bullets: Solutions to climate, culture, and space
